Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A compound barbell press performed lying on a flat bench, mainly building the mid chest, front shoulders, and triceps.
Help: 1. Lie on the bench with eyes under the bar, feet flat on the floor. 2. Grip slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack the bar. 3. Lower it under control to mid-chest. 4. Press back up to full lock-out. Tip: keep shoulder blades pinned back and don't bounce the bar off your chest.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A cable version of the chest press that keeps constant tension on the pectorals through the whole range of motion.
Help: 1. Set both pulleys to chest height and stand in the middle. 2. Grab a handle in each hand and step forward slightly. 3. Press handles forward until arms extend. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: keep a slight forward lean and squeeze your chest at full extension instead of just locking the elbows.

Tags: Chest, Lower Chest, Pectoralis Major
Description: A cable fly performed from a high pulley angle downward, emphasizing the lower chest fibers.
Help: 1. Set pulleys above head height and grab a handle in each hand. 2. Step forward with a slight forward lean and soft elbow bend. 3. Pull handles down and across in an arc to meet in front of your hips. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: keep the arc motion controlled and avoid using momentum or locking the elbows.

Tags: Chest, Upper Chest, Clavicular Head, Pectoralis Major
Description: A cable fly performed from a low pulley angle upward, targeting the upper chest and clavicular head.
Help: 1. Set pulleys low and grab a handle in each hand. 2. Step forward with a slight forward lean. 3. Pull handles up and across in an arc to meet above chest height. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: drive through the upper chest and keep the movement an arc, not a straight-line press.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major
Description: A cable fly with pulleys set at chest height, isolating the mid chest through a wide arcing motion.
Help: 1. Set both pulleys to chest height and grab a handle in each hand. 2. Step forward with a slight forward lean and soft elbow bend. 3. Bring handles together in front of your chest in an arc. 4. Return slowly, feeling a stretch across the chest. Tip: keep elbows softly bent throughout and don't let the weight pull your arms back too far.

Tags: Chest, Lower Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps, Anterior Deltoid
Description: A bodyweight dip leaning forward on parallel bars, heavily loading the lower chest and triceps.
Help: 1. Grip the parallel bars and lift yourself up with arms extended. 2. Lean your torso forward and bend your knees. 3. Lower yourself until you feel a stretch in the chest. 4. Press back up to the top. Tip: lean forward to bias the chest, and avoid dropping too deep if you feel shoulder strain.

Tags: Chest, Lower Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps
Description: A barbell or dumbbell press on a decline bench that emphasizes the lower portion of the pectoralis major.
Help: 1. Secure your legs and lie back on the decline bench. 2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width. 3. Lower the bar to your lower chest. 4. Press back up to lock-out. Tip: control the descent since the decline angle can make the bar path feel less stable.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps
Description: A push-up performed with hands elevated on blocks or handles, increasing the range of motion for the mid chest and triceps.
Help: 1. Place hands on two elevated platforms shoulder-width apart. 2. Get into a straight-body plank position. 3. Lower your chest below hand level for a deep stretch. 4. Push back up to full extension. Tip: keep your core tight so hips don't sag as you go deeper than a standard push-up.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps
Description: A flat press using dumbbells that trains the mid chest and triceps while allowing a greater range of motion than a barbell.
Help: 1. Sit on the bench with a dumbbell on each thigh, then lie back kicking them up to chest level. 2. Position dumbbells at chest height, palms forward. 3. Press up until arms are extended. 4. Lower slowly back to chest level. Tip: keep wrists stacked over elbows and avoid letting the dumbbells drift too far apart or together.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major
Description: An isolation exercise lying on a bench, arcing dumbbells out and up to stretch and squeeze the mid chest.
Help: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest, palms facing in. 2. Slightly bend your elbows and keep them fixed. 3. Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in an arc until you feel a chest stretch. 4. Bring them back together above your chest. Tip: keep the elbow bend constant throughout to protect the shoulder joint.

Tags: Chest, Lower Chest, Latissimus Dorsi
Description: A lying dumbbell movement that stretches and works the lower chest and lats together.
Help: 1. Lie perpendicular across a bench with only your upper back supported. 2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands above your chest, arms slightly bent. 3. Lower the dumbbell back and behind your head in an arc. 4. Pull it back over your chest to the start. Tip: keep hips low and core braced so you don't arch excessively as the weight moves overhead.

Tags: Chest, Upper Chest, Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A push-up with feet raised on a bench or box, shifting more load onto the upper chest and front shoulders.
Help: 1. Place your feet on an elevated surface and hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulders. 2. Form a straight line from shoulders to ankles. 3. Lower your chest toward the floor. 4. Push back up to full extension. Tip: keep hips in line with shoulders, don't let them sag or pike up.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps
Description: A pressing movement performed lying on the floor, limiting range of motion to protect shoulders while building mid chest and triceps.
Help: 1. Lie on the floor with knees bent, holding a barbell or dumbbells above your chest. 2. Lower until your upper arms touch the floor. 3. Pause briefly. 4. Press back up to lock-out. Tip: the floor stops the descent early, so use it to work on lockout strength and avoid shoulder overstretching.

Tags: Chest, Upper Chest, Clavicular Head, Anterior Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A barbell press on an inclined bench that shifts emphasis to the upper chest and front shoulders.
Help: 1. Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline and lie back. 2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and unrack it. 3. Lower the bar to your upper chest. 4. Press back up to full extension. Tip: avoid setting the incline too steep or the shoulders take over from the chest.

Tags: Chest, Upper Chest, Clavicular Head, Anterior Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A dumbbell press on an incline bench targeting the upper chest, clavicular head, and front shoulders.
Help: 1. Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline and sit with a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height. 2. Lie back keeping the dumbbells at chest level, palms forward. 3. Press up until arms extend. 4. Lower slowly back to the start. Tip: keep the incline moderate and control the weights instead of letting them drift toward your face.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps
Description: A modified push-up performed from the knees, training the mid chest and triceps with reduced load for beginners.
Help: 1. Kneel on a mat with hands slightly wider than shoulders. 2. Keep a straight line from head to knees. 3. Lower your chest toward the floor. 4. Push back up to full extension. Tip: keep hips from sagging so the movement stays a true push-up pattern, not a lower back exercise.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps
Description: A guided machine press that trains the mid chest and triceps along a fixed, stable pressing path.
Help: 1. Adjust the seat so handles align with mid-chest height. 2. Grip the handles with a neutral or pronated grip. 3. Press forward until arms are extended. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: adjust seat height first so the movement mimics a natural bench press path, not an overhead angle.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major
Description: A machine isolation exercise that brings the arms together in front of the chest to target the mid chest.
Help: 1. Adjust the seat so handles are at chest height. 2. Grip the handles or place forearms on the pads with elbows slightly bent. 3. Bring your arms together in front of your chest. 4. Return slowly to the stretched position. Tip: avoid slamming the pads together, control the squeeze and the stretch equally.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Triceps, Core
Description: A classic bodyweight press trained on the floor, working the mid chest, triceps, shoulders, and core.
Help: 1. Place hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight plank line. 2. Brace your core and glutes. 3. Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows at about 45 degrees. 4. Push back up to full extension. Tip: keep your body rigid from head to heels, don't let hips sag or pike.

Tags: Chest, Serratus Anterior
Description: A push-up variation adding a scapular protraction at the top, emphasizing the serratus anterior.
Help: 1. Get into a standard push-up position. 2. Perform a normal push-up down and up. 3. At the top, push your upper back further up, rounding it slightly, spreading the shoulder blades apart. 4. Return to the normal top position and repeat. Tip: keep arms straight during the plus phase, the movement comes from the shoulder blades, not the elbows.

Tags: Chest, Mid Chest, Pectoralis Major, Anterior Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A guided-bar-path bench press on the Smith machine, building mid chest, front shoulders, and triceps with added stability.
Help: 1. Set the bench under the fixed bar path and lie flat. 2. Unhook the bar with a grip slightly wider than shoulders. 3. Lower the bar to mid-chest. 4. Press back up and re-hook when finished. Tip: position the bench so the bar naturally lines up over your mid-chest, since the path is fixed vertically.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii
Description: A machine or band-assisted vertical pull that builds the lats and biceps while reducing the bodyweight lifted.
Help: 1. Set the assistance level and kneel or stand on the platform/band. 2. Grip the bar with hands shoulder-width or wider. 3. Pull your chest toward the bar, driving elbows down. 4. Lower under control to full arm extension. Tip: reduce assistance gradually over time rather than relying on the same support level indefinitely.

Tags: Back, Erector Spinae, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
Description: A hip-hinge exercise on an extension bench that strengthens the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings.
Help: 1. Position hips on the pad with ankles secured, body straight. 2. Cross arms over your chest or hold weight. 3. Lower your torso down by hinging at the hips. 4. Raise back up to a straight line, without hyperextending. Tip: stop at a flat back position at the top, don't arch the lower back excessively.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Trapezius
Description: A hinged barbell row that builds the mid back, lats, rhomboids, and trapezius through a horizontal pulling motion.
Help: 1. Hinge at the hips holding a barbell with hands shoulder-width apart, back flat. 2. Let the bar hang below your shoulders. 3. Pull the bar up toward your lower ribs, driving elbows back. 4. Lower under control to the start. Tip: keep your back flat and braced throughout, don't round it to move heavier weight.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Latissimus Dorsi
Description: A machine row where the chest rests on a pad, isolating the mid back and lats without lower back strain.
Help: 1. Adjust the seat and chest pad so handles are at chest height. 2. Sit with chest against the pad and grip the handles. 3. Pull the handles toward your torso, squeezing shoulder blades together. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: keep your chest pressed into the pad the whole time to avoid using body momentum.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Middle Trapezius, Rhomboids, Latissimus Dorsi
Description: A T-bar row performed with chest support, targeting the mid back, rhomboids, and lats with a stable base.
Help: 1. Lie chest-down on the support pad and grip the handles. 2. Let the weight hang with arms extended. 3. Pull the handles up toward your torso, squeezing your shoulder blades. 4. Lower under control to the start. Tip: keep the chest anchored on the pad so the pull comes from the back, not from swinging the torso.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis
Description: A vertical pull with an underhand grip that heavily recruits the lats, biceps, and brachialis.
Help: 1. Grip the bar with palms facing you, shoulder-width apart. 2. Hang with arms fully extended. 3. Pull your chin over the bar, driving elbows down and back. 4. Lower under control to full extension. Tip: avoid kipping or swinging, control the descent to keep tension on the lats and biceps.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Lower Lats
Description: A lat pulldown using a close or neutral grip attachment, emphasizing the lower lats and biceps.
Help: 1. Sit at the pulldown station and secure your knees under the pad. 2. Grip the close or neutral handle. 3. Pull the handle down to your upper chest, driving elbows down and back. 4. Return slowly to full arm extension. Tip: avoid leaning back excessively, keep the torso mostly upright and pull with your back.

Tags: Back, Erector Spinae, Trapezius, Latissimus Dorsi, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings, Lower Back, Glutes
Description: A full-body hip-hinge lift from the floor that builds the erector spinae, glutes, hamstrings, traps, and lats.
Help: 1. Stand with the bar over mid-foot, feet hip-width apart. 2. Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your knees, back flat, chest up. 3. Drive through your feet, extending hips and knees together to stand tall. 4. Lower the bar back down under control by hinging first. Tip: keep the bar close to your legs throughout and never let your lower back round under load.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Middle Trapezius, Rhomboids
Description: A bodyweight horizontal pull under a bar or rack, working the mid back, lats, and trapezius.
Help: 1. Set a bar at hip height and lie underneath it, gripping it shoulder-width apart. 2. Extend legs out with body in a straight line, heels on the floor. 3. Pull your chest up toward the bar, squeezing shoulder blades. 4. Lower under control to the start. Tip: keep your body rigid and straight, don't let your hips sag toward the floor.

Tags: Back, Upper Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Trapezius
Description: A machine row pulling from a high angle, targeting the upper back, lats, rhomboids, and trapezius.
Help: 1. Adjust the seat so handles are above chest height. 2. Grip the handles and sit tall against the pad. 3. Pull the handles down and back toward your upper chest. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: focus on driving elbows down and back rather than just bending the arms.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Middle Trapezius
Description: A single-arm cable row that builds the lats, rhomboids, and mid trapezius with an added core and anti-rotation demand.
Help: 1. Attach a single handle to a low cable and sit or stand facing it. 2. Grip the handle with one hand, arm extended. 3. Pull the handle back toward your ribs, rotating your torso slightly if standing. 4. Return under control to the start. Tip: avoid twisting excessively, let the movement come from the back and shoulder blade.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Middle Trapezius, Mid Back
Description: A single-arm row supported by a bench, isolating the lats, rhomboids, and mid trapezius on each side.
Help: 1. Place one knee and hand on a bench, back flat, holding a dumbbell in the other hand. 2. Let the dumbbell hang straight down. 3. Pull it up toward your hip, driving the elbow back. 4. Lower under control to full extension. Tip: keep your torso still and avoid rotating your spine to lift the weight.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Trapezius, Erector Spinae
Description: An explosive barbell row starting each rep from a dead stop on the floor, building the mid back, lats, and erector spinae.
Help: 1. Hinge over a barbell on the floor with a flat back, torso close to parallel. 2. Grip the bar shoulder-width apart. 3. Pull the bar explosively to your lower chest. 4. Lower it back to the floor fully between reps. Tip: reset your position for every rep instead of letting the bar hover, this keeps the back flat and strict.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Teres Major, Biceps Brachii
Description: A vertical bodyweight pull with an overhand grip that primarily targets the lats, teres major, and biceps.
Help: 1. Grip the bar with palms facing away, hands wider than shoulders. 2. Hang with arms fully extended. 3. Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar, driving elbows down. 4. Lower under control to full extension. Tip: avoid excessive kipping, control both the pull and the lowering phase.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Rhomboids, Latissimus Dorsi, Middle Trapezius
Description: A seated cable pull that trains the mid back, rhomboids, lats, and middle trapezius with a stable seated base.
Help: 1. Sit at the cable row station with feet on the platform, knees slightly bent. 2. Grip the handle with arms extended and back straight. 3. Pull the handle to your torso, squeezing shoulder blades together. 4. Return slowly, letting your torso lean slightly forward. Tip: keep your torso mostly upright and avoid using body swing to move the weight.

Tags: Back, Upper Trapezius
Description: A shrugging movement using the Smith machine's fixed bar path to isolate the upper trapezius.
Help: 1. Stand under the bar, gripping it at shoulder-width, arms straight. 2. Unrack the bar and stand tall. 3. Elevate your shoulders straight up toward your ears. 4. Lower under control back to the start. Tip: avoid rolling the shoulders, the motion is a straight vertical shrug to protect the shoulder joint.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Teres Major
Description: An isolation pulldown with straight arms that targets the lats and teres major without engaging the biceps much.
Help: 1. Stand facing a high cable with a straight bar attachment, arms extended. 2. Hinge slightly forward at the hips. 3. Pull the bar down toward your thighs, keeping arms straight. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: keep elbows only slightly bent and fixed throughout so the lats do the work, not the triceps.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Biceps Brachii
Description: A lat pulldown using an underhand grip, emphasizing the lats along with strong biceps involvement.
Help: 1. Sit at the pulldown station and secure your knees under the pad. 2. Grip the bar underhand, shoulder-width apart. 3. Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving elbows down. 4. Return slowly to full arm extension. Tip: avoid leaning back too far, keep the pull controlled and let the elbows travel down and back.

Tags: Back, Mid Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Trapezius
Description: A loaded row using a T-bar or landmine setup that builds the mid back, lats, rhomboids, and trapezius.
Help: 1. Straddle the bar, hinge at the hips with a flat back. 2. Grip the handles with arms extended. 3. Pull the weight up toward your torso, squeezing shoulder blades. 4. Lower under control to the start. Tip: keep your back flat and braced, don't round it to heave the weight up.

Tags: Back, Latissimus Dorsi, Teres Major, Upper Lats
Description: A lat pulldown using a wide overhand grip that emphasizes the lats, teres major, and upper lats.
Help: 1. Sit at the pulldown station and secure your knees under the pad. 2. Grip the bar wide, palms facing away. 3. Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving elbows down and back. 4. Return slowly to full arm extension. Tip: avoid using momentum by leaning back too far, keep the movement controlled and strict.

Tags: Shoulders, Anterior Deltoid, Medial Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A dumbbell shoulder press variant with a rotating grip that trains all three deltoid heads plus triceps.
Help: 1. Sit holding dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you. 2. Press up while rotating palms to face forward. 3. Lock out overhead, then reverse the rotation on the way down. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Keep the rotation smooth and controlled, don't rush it to swing the weights up.

Tags: Shoulders, Rotator Cuff, Infraspinatus, Teres Minor
Description: An isolation exercise using a low cable to strengthen the rotator cuff, especially the infraspinatus and teres minor.
Help: 1. Stand side-on to the cable with elbow bent 90 degrees and tucked to your side. 2. Hold the handle at waist height. 3. Rotate the forearm outward away from your body, keeping the elbow pinned to your ribs. 4. Return slowly and repeat. Tip: Use light weight and keep the elbow fixed; this is a control exercise, not a strength lift.

Tags: Shoulders, Posterior Deltoid, External Rotators, Middle Trapezius, Trapezius
Description: A cable pulling exercise for the rear deltoids and upper back that also strengthens external rotators and improves shoulder health.
Help: 1. Set a rope attachment at upper chest to head height. 2. Grip the ends and step back for tension. 3. Pull the rope toward your face, splitting hands apart and driving elbows high and wide. 4. Squeeze the shoulder blades, then return slowly. Tip: Lead with the elbows and externally rotate at the end, don't just pull with the arms.

Tags: Shoulders, Medial Deltoid
Description: A cable isolation move targeting the medial deltoid to build shoulder width, with constant tension throughout the range.
Help: 1. Stand side-on to a low cable pulley, handle in the far hand. 2. Keep a slight elbow bend. 3. Raise the arm out to the side until roughly shoulder height. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Lead with the elbow, not the hand, and avoid shrugging the trap to lift the weight.

Tags: Shoulders, Posterior Deltoid, Middle Trapezius
Description: A cable exercise isolating the posterior deltoid and mid-back muscles to improve shoulder balance and posture.
Help: 1. Set two cables at chest height, cross the handles to opposite hands. 2. Stand centered with a slight forward lean. 3. Sweep the arms out and back in a wide arc, squeezing the shoulder blades. 4. Return slowly and repeat. Tip: Keep elbows slightly bent and avoid using momentum or heavy weight that shortens the range.

Tags: Shoulders, Anterior Deltoid
Description: An isolation exercise that targets the anterior (front) deltoid by raising dumbbells forward to shoulder height.
Help: 1. Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms facing in. 2. Keep a slight elbow bend and core braced. 3. Raise one or both arms forward to shoulder height. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Avoid swinging the weight up with momentum or leaning back to cheat the rep.

Tags: Shoulders, Medial Deltoid
Description: A classic isolation exercise for the medial deltoid that builds shoulder width by raising dumbbells out to the sides.
Help: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in. 2. Keep a slight elbow bend. 3. Raise both arms out to the sides to about shoulder height. 4. Lower slowly and repeat. Tip: Lead with the elbows and stop before shrugging the traps take over.

Tags: Shoulders, Posterior Deltoid, Trapezius
Description: A bent-over isolation move that targets the posterior deltoid and upper back muscles for balanced shoulder development.
Help: 1. Hinge at the hips holding dumbbells with a soft knee bend. 2. Let the arms hang with a slight elbow bend. 3. Raise the weights out to the sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep the back flat and avoid using momentum from rocking the torso.

Tags: Shoulders, Anterior Deltoid, Medial Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A pressing exercise using a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment, building shoulder and triceps strength with less joint stress.
Help: 1. Hold the barbell end at shoulder height with one or both hands. 2. Brace your core and stagger your stance. 3. Press the bar up and slightly forward along its arc. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Let the bar travel its natural arc rather than pressing it straight overhead.

Tags: Shoulders, Medial Deltoid
Description: A machine-based isolation exercise that targets the medial deltoid with a fixed, supported movement path.
Help: 1. Sit with the pads against the outside of your upper arms and torso against the back pad. 2. Set a moderate weight. 3. Raise the arms out to shoulder height. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Avoid using your shoulders to shrug the weight up; let the delts do the work.

Tags: Shoulders, Anterior Deltoid, Medial Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A bodyweight pressing exercise in a bent-over V position that emphasizes the shoulders and triceps.
Help: 1. Start in a downward-dog position, hips high, hands shoulder-width apart. 2. Bend the elbows to lower your head toward the floor. 3. Press back up to the start. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Keep hips high throughout so the load stays on the shoulders rather than the chest.

Exercise: Reverse Pec Deck / Machine Rear Delt Fly
Tags: Shoulders, Posterior Deltoid, Rhomboids, Middle Trapezius
Description: A machine exercise isolating the posterior deltoid and rhomboids by pulling the arms backward against pads.
Help: 1. Sit facing the pad with chest against it, grip the handles. 2. Keep a slight elbow bend. 3. Pull the arms out and back in an arc, squeezing the shoulder blades. 4. Return slowly and repeat. Tip: Keep the movement controlled; don't let the weight stack slam on the return.

Tags: Shoulders, Anterior Deltoid, Medial Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A compound overhead pressing exercise that builds the anterior and medial deltoids along with the triceps.
Help: 1. Sit with back supported, holding dumbbells or a barbell at shoulder height. 2. Brace your core. 3. Press the weight straight overhead until arms are extended. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Avoid excessive lower back arch; keep ribs down and press in a straight vertical line.

Tags: Shoulders, Anterior Deltoid, Medial Deltoid, Triceps
Description: A guided-bar variation of the overhead press that trains the deltoids and triceps with a fixed movement path.
Help: 1. Sit or stand under the bar with a shoulder-width grip. 2. Unrack and lower the bar to upper chest or chin level. 3. Press it back up to full elbow extension. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Position the bench so the bar path stays in line with your shoulders, not out in front.

Tags: Shoulders, Serratus Anterior, Lower Trapezius
Description: A mobility and activation drill for the shoulders that improves scapular control and posture using the serratus anterior and lower trapezius.
Help: 1. Stand with back, head and arms against a wall, elbows and wrists touching it. 2. Slide the arms upward as high as possible while keeping contact. 3. Slide back down to the start. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Keep ribs down and lower back flat against the wall to avoid arching.

Tags: Shoulders, Lower Trapezius, Posterior Deltoid, Serratus Anterior
Description: A light raise performed lying face-down or on an incline bench that strengthens the lower trapezius and posterior deltoid for better shoulder posture.
Help: 1. Lie face-down on an incline bench or floor, arms hanging with thumbs up. 2. Raise the arms overhead in a Y shape. 3. Squeeze the upper back at the top. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Use very light weight; this exercise is about control and scapular movement, not load.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Biceps Short Head, Biceps Long Head
Description: A classic compound biceps exercise using a barbell or EZ-bar to build overall biceps mass and strength.
Help: 1. Stand holding the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip. 2. Keep elbows tucked at your sides. 3. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Avoid swinging your torso or flaring elbows forward to cheat the weight up.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Biceps Long Head
Description: A cable curl performed standing away from a low pulley with the arm behind the body, emphasizing the long head of the biceps through a stretched position.
Help: 1. Stand facing away from a low cable, arm extended behind you. 2. Keep the elbow slightly back and fixed. 3. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder. 4. Lower slowly to feel the stretch. Tip: Keep the elbow pinned behind your torso; letting it drift forward reduces the stretch benefit.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Biceps Short Head, Biceps Long Head
Description: A cable-based biceps curl using a straight bar attachment that keeps constant tension on the biceps through the full range.
Help: 1. Stand facing a low pulley, gripping the straight bar underhand. 2. Keep elbows tucked at your sides. 3. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep the tension on the biceps by not locking out or resting at the bottom.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Biceps Short Head
Description: A cable curl performed on a preacher bench that isolates the biceps by fixing the upper arm and removing momentum.
Help: 1. Set the preacher pad in front of a low cable pulley. 2. Rest the back of your upper arm on the pad, gripping the handle. 3. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder. 4. Lower slowly without letting the arm fully slam straight. Tip: Don't let the elbow lift off the pad; that shifts work away from the biceps.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Brachioradialis, Biceps Long Head
Description: A neutral-grip cable curl using a rope attachment that targets the biceps, brachialis and forearms.
Help: 1. Stand facing a low pulley holding the rope ends with palms facing each other. 2. Keep elbows tucked at your sides. 3. Curl the rope up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep your wrists neutral throughout; don't let them rotate as you curl.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Biceps Short Head
Description: A single-arm dumbbell curl performed seated with the elbow braced against the inner thigh for strict biceps isolation.
Help: 1. Sit on a bench, lean forward, and brace your elbow against the inside of your thigh. 2. Hold a dumbbell with an underhand grip, arm extended. 3. Curl the weight up toward your shoulder. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep the upper arm still throughout; only the forearm should move.

Tags: Biceps, Brachialis, Brachioradialis
Description: A dumbbell curl where the weight is brought across the body toward the opposite shoulder, emphasizing the brachialis and brachioradialis.
Help: 1. Stand holding a dumbbell with a neutral grip at your side. 2. Keep the elbow tucked. 3. Curl the dumbbell up and across your body toward the opposite shoulder. 4. Lower under control and repeat on both sides. Tip: Keep the elbow pinned to your ribs so the shoulder doesn't assist the lift.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Brachioradialis, Biceps Long Head
Description: A neutral-grip dumbbell curl that emphasizes the brachialis and brachioradialis alongside the biceps.
Help: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides with palms facing each other. 2. Keep elbows tucked. 3. Curl both weights up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep wrists straight and neutral throughout, don't let them rotate into a regular curl.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis
Description: A single-arm or double-arm dumbbell curl on a preacher bench that isolates the biceps by eliminating swing.
Help: 1. Rest the back of your upper arm on a preacher pad, holding a dumbbell underhand. 2. Extend the arm fully at the bottom. 3. Curl the weight up toward your shoulder. 4. Lower slowly and repeat. Tip: Don't let the elbow lift off the pad or fully hyperextend at the bottom.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis
Description: A preacher-bench curl using an EZ-bar that isolates the biceps while easing wrist strain with its angled grip.
Help: 1. Rest your upper arms on the preacher pad, gripping the EZ-bar underhand. 2. Extend the arms at the bottom without locking out hard. 3. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position; control the descent.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Biceps Long Head
Description: A curl performed lying back on an incline bench that stretches the long head of the biceps for greater emphasis.
Help: 1. Lie back on an incline bench, arms hanging straight down holding dumbbells. 2. Keep elbows back, in line with your torso. 3. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control, feeling the stretch. Tip: Resist letting your elbows drift forward, which reduces the stretch and shifts tension off the biceps.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis
Description: A machine-guided curl that isolates the biceps with a fixed path, useful for consistent tension and less stabilization demand.
Help: 1. Sit and adjust the seat so your elbows align with the machine's pivot. 2. Grip the handles. 3. Curl the handles up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep your upper arms pressed against the pad throughout the movement.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis, Biceps Short Head
Description: A machine version of the preacher curl that isolates the biceps, particularly the short head, with a supported upper arm.
Help: 1. Sit and rest your upper arms on the machine's preacher pad. 2. Grip the handles with an underhand grip. 3. Curl the handles up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower slowly and repeat. Tip: Keep the movement slow on the way down; don't let the weight stack drop quickly.

Tags: Biceps, Brachialis, Brachioradialis, Forearms
Description: A curl performed with an overhand grip that shifts emphasis to the brachialis, brachioradialis and forearm extensors.
Help: 1. Stand holding a barbell or EZ-bar with an overhand, shoulder-width grip. 2. Keep elbows tucked at your sides. 3. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Use lighter weight than a regular curl since the grip is mechanically weaker.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis
Description: A seated variation of the dumbbell curl that removes leg drive and body momentum for stricter biceps work.
Help: 1. Sit on a bench holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing forward. 2. Keep elbows tucked. 3. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Sitting removes the ability to swing your legs or torso for momentum, so keep reps strict.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii
Description: A curl performed with the cable set high, pulling the arm down and in toward the body to target the biceps peak.
Help: 1. Stand between or beside a high pulley, arm extended out to the side. 2. Keep the elbow elevated and fixed. 3. Curl the handle down and in toward your shoulder. 4. Return slowly and repeat. Tip: Keep the elbow height steady throughout; don't let it drop as you fatigue.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Biceps Short Head
Description: A curl performed lying face-down on an incline bench with arms hanging free, isolating the biceps short head.
Help: 1. Lie face-down on an incline bench, arms hanging straight down holding a bar or dumbbells. 2. Keep upper arms still. 3. Curl the weight up toward your shoulders. 4. Lower under control without swinging. Tip: Avoid letting the elbows move forward or back; only the forearms should travel.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachialis
Description: A standing curl performed one arm at a time, alternating sides, to build biceps size and strength.
Help: 1. Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms facing in. 2. Curl one arm up while rotating the palm to face up. 3. Lower that arm as you curl the other. 4. Alternate for reps. Tip: Keep the non-working arm still and avoid leaning side to side to assist the lift.

Tags: Biceps, Biceps Brachii, Brachioradialis, Forearms
Description: A curl that combines a regular curl up with a reverse-grip lowering, working both the biceps and forearm muscles.
Help: 1. Stand holding dumbbells with palms facing forward. 2. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders. 3. Rotate your palms to face down at the top. 4. Lower slowly in that reversed grip, then rotate back and repeat. Tip: Control the lowering phase slowly since that's what builds the forearms.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii
Description: A single-arm cable isolation exercise that extends the arm behind the body to target the triceps.
Help: 1. Attach a handle to a low cable, hinge forward at the hips, and tuck your upper arm against your torso. 2. Bend the elbow to about 90 degrees. 3. Extend the arm straight back, squeezing the triceps. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep the upper arm still and parallel to the floor; only the forearm should move.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Chest, Anterior Deltoid
Description: A bench press variation with a narrower grip that shifts emphasis from the chest to the triceps.
Help: 1. Lie on a bench and grip the bar just inside shoulder width. 2. Unrack and lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows tucked. 3. Press the bar back up to full extension. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Keep elbows tracking close to your body rather than flaring out to protect the wrists and shoulders.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii
Description: A single-arm cable extension pulling the handle down and across the body, isolating the triceps through a varied angle.
Help: 1. Stand beside a high cable, grip the handle with the working arm across your body. 2. Keep the upper arm fixed. 3. Extend the arm down and across until straight. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep the elbow close to your body and avoid using the shoulder to swing the weight.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii
Description: A single-arm dumbbell isolation exercise that extends the arm backward to target the triceps.
Help: 1. Hinge forward, supporting yourself with one hand on a bench, holding a dumbbell in the other. 2. Keep the upper arm parallel to the floor. 3. Extend the arm straight back, squeezing the triceps. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Avoid swinging the weight; keep the upper arm still and let only the forearm move.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Long Head
Description: An overhead pressing-style isolation exercise using a dumbbell that stretches and targets the long head of the triceps.
Help: 1. Sit or stand holding a dumbbell overhead with both hands, arms extended. 2. Keep elbows pointing forward and close together. 3. Lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows. 4. Extend back up and repeat. Tip: Keep elbows still and pointing forward throughout; don't let them flare outward.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Chest, Triceps Lateral Head
Description: A hybrid movement between a close-grip bench press and a skull crusher that heavily loads the triceps.
Help: 1. Lie on a bench with a close, overhand grip on the bar. 2. Lower the bar toward your neck or upper chest, bending the elbows. 3. Press the bar back up and slightly back to lockout. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Start with lighter weight to learn the bar path safely before adding load.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Long Head
Description: An isolation exercise performed lying on a bench, lowering dumbbells toward the head to stretch and work the triceps.
Help: 1. Lie on a bench holding dumbbells extended above your chest. 2. Keep upper arms still, elbows pointing up. 3. Lower the weights toward your ears by bending the elbows. 4. Extend back up and repeat. Tip: Keep elbows tucked in rather than flaring out to keep tension on the triceps.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Chest, Anterior Deltoid
Description: A machine-guided dip that trains the triceps along with the chest and front shoulders through a supported pressing motion.
Help: 1. Sit and grip the handles with arms bent. 2. Brace your core and keep torso upright for triceps emphasis. 3. Press the handles down until arms are extended. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep the torso upright rather than leaning forward, which shifts more work to the chest.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii
Description: A machine-based isolation exercise that trains the triceps through a fixed, supported extension path.
Help: 1. Sit and adjust the seat so your elbows align with the pivot point. 2. Grip the handles with upper arms resting against the pad. 3. Extend your arms down until straight. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep upper arms pinned to the pad; don't let them lift as you push.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii
Description: A cable pushdown performed with an underhand grip that shifts emphasis toward the inner and long head of the triceps.
Help: 1. Stand facing a high cable with a straight bar, gripping underhand. 2. Keep elbows tucked at your sides. 3. Push the bar down until arms are fully extended. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep elbows fixed at your sides throughout; don't let them drift forward.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Long Head
Description: An overhead cable extension using a rope attachment that stretches and isolates the long head of the triceps.
Help: 1. Face away from a low cable, rope overhead, elbows pointing forward. 2. Keep upper arms still. 3. Extend the arms forward and up until straight. 4. Return under control, feeling the stretch. Tip: Keep elbows close together and pointing forward instead of flaring out.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Lateral Head
Description: A cable pushdown using a rope attachment, allowing the hands to split apart at the bottom for a stronger triceps contraction.
Help: 1. Stand facing a high cable with a rope attachment, elbows tucked at your sides. 2. Push the rope down until arms are extended. 3. Spread the rope ends apart and turn palms down at the bottom. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep elbows pinned to your sides; only the forearms should move.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Lateral Head
Description: A one-arm cable pushdown variation that isolates each triceps individually and helps fix side-to-side strength imbalances.
Help: 1. Stand facing a high cable with a single handle, elbow tucked at your side. 2. Keep the upper arm still. 3. Push the handle down until the arm is fully extended. 4. Return under control and repeat on both sides. Tip: Avoid twisting your torso to help push the weight down.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Long Head
Description: A one-arm overhead cable extension that stretches and isolates the long head of the triceps on each side individually.
Help: 1. Face away from a low cable, holding the handle overhead with one arm, elbow pointing forward. 2. Keep the upper arm still. 3. Extend the arm up until straight. 4. Return under control, feeling the stretch. Tip: Keep the elbow pointing forward and stationary; don't let it drift outward.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Long Head
Description: A lying triceps isolation exercise where the bar is lowered toward the forehead, then pressed back up.
Help: 1. Lie on a bench holding an EZ-bar or barbell above your chest, arms extended. 2. Keep upper arms still, elbows pointing up. 3. Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending the elbows. 4. Extend back up and repeat. Tip: Move slowly and keep elbows fixed in place; this exercise is unforgiving of sloppy control.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Lateral Head
Description: A cable pushdown using a straight bar that trains the triceps, especially the lateral head, with a fixed grip path.
Help: 1. Stand facing a high cable with a straight bar, overhand grip, elbows tucked. 2. Keep the upper arms still. 3. Push the bar down until arms are fully extended. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Keep elbows pinned to your sides throughout; don't let them travel forward as you push.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Triceps Lateral Head
Description: A cable pushdown using a V-bar attachment with a neutral grip that trains the triceps with strong lockout emphasis.
Help: 1. Stand facing a high cable with a V-bar, neutral grip, elbows tucked at your sides. 2. Keep the upper arms still. 3. Push the bar down until arms are fully extended. 4. Return under control and repeat. Tip: Squeeze hard at full extension rather than just touching lockout.

Tags: Triceps, Triceps Brachii, Chest, Anterior Deltoid
Description: A compound pressing exercise using added weight that heavily loads the triceps along with the chest and front shoulders.
Help: 1. Support yourself on parallel bars, arms extended, added weight attached via belt or held between the legs. 2. Lower your body by bending the elbows, keeping torso upright for triceps focus. 3. Press back up to full extension. 4. Repeat for reps. Tip: Avoid dipping too deep if you feel shoulder strain; keep torso upright rather than leaning forward.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Adductor Magnus, Glutes
Description: A compound squat with a barbell across the upper back that builds quadriceps, glutes, and overall lower-body strength.
Help: 1. Set the bar on your upper traps, feet shoulder-width apart. 2. Brace your core and unrack the bar. 3. Bend hips and knees to lower until thighs are at least parallel to the floor. 4. Drive through your heels to stand back up. Tip: Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes throughout.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
Description: A floor-based hip extension exercise with a barbell across the hips that isolates the glutes and hamstrings.
Help: 1. Sit with upper back against a bench, barbell over hips, knees bent. 2. Plant feet flat, shoulder-width apart. 3. Drive through heels to lift hips until torso is level with thighs. 4. Squeeze glutes at the top, then lower with control. Tip: Avoid overarching your lower back; tuck your chin and keep ribs down.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
Description: A bench-supported hip extension movement with a loaded barbell that heavily targets the glutes.
Help: 1. Rest upper back on a bench, barbell padded across hip crease. 2. Plant feet flat, knees bent about 90 degrees. 3. Drive through heels to raise hips until torso is parallel to floor. 4. Pause and squeeze glutes hard, then lower under control. Tip: Keep chin tucked and avoid hyperextending the lower back at the top.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus
Description: A squat variation loaded through a belt at the hips instead of the spine, targeting quads and glutes with less back stress.
Help: 1. Attach the belt around your hips and step onto the platform. 2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. 3. Bend knees and hips to squat down until thighs are parallel to the floor. 4. Push through your feet to return to standing. Tip: Keep your torso upright since the load hangs below you, not on your spine.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings, Glutes
Description: A single-leg squat with the rear foot elevated behind you, building quad, glute, and hamstring strength while challenging balance.
Help: 1. Stand a couple feet in front of a bench, rest one foot behind you on it. 2. Lower your back knee toward the floor by bending the front leg. 3. Keep most of your weight on the front foot. 4. Push through the front heel to rise back up. Tip: Keep your torso upright and don't let the front knee cave inward.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Maximus
Description: An isolation exercise using a cable or machine to extend one leg backward, targeting the glutes directly.
Help: 1. Attach an ankle cuff to the cable and clip it to one ankle. 2. Hold the frame for support, hinge slightly forward. 3. Kick the working leg straight back and up, squeezing the glute. 4. Return with control without letting the weight stack touch down. Tip: Avoid arching your lower back to gain range; keep the motion coming from the hip.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Medius, Gluteus Minimus
Description: A standing cable exercise that moves the leg outward to the side, isolating the gluteus medius and minimus.
Help: 1. Attach a cuff to your ankle, cable anchored low from the opposite side. 2. Stand tall, holding the frame for balance. 3. Sweep the working leg out to the side against resistance. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: Keep your torso still and avoid leaning to swing the leg using momentum.

Tags: Legs, Calves, Gastrocnemius, Soleus
Description: A calf isolation exercise performed on the leg press machine, pressing through the balls of the feet to train the calves.
Help: 1. Sit in the leg press with legs extended, balls of feet on the lower edge of the platform. 2. Let heels drop below the platform edge for a stretch. 3. Press through the balls of your feet to extend your ankles fully. 4. Lower under control and repeat. Tip: Keep knees slightly bent and locked in place; the movement should come only from the ankles.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Maximus, Quadriceps
Description: A lateral step-up where the working foot crosses in front of the body onto a raised platform, targeting glutes and quads.
Help: 1. Stand beside a box or bench with one foot near it. 2. Cross the near foot over and place it fully on top of the box. 3. Drive through that foot to step up, bringing the other leg up. 4. Step back down with control and repeat. Tip: Keep the stepping knee tracking over the foot, not caving inward.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus
Description: A single-leg step-forward exercise that trains the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings while challenging balance.
Help: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. 2. Step forward with one leg and lower your hips. 3. Bend both knees until the back knee nears the floor. 4. Push through the front heel to return to standing. Tip: Keep your front knee tracking over your ankle, not past your toes.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Adductor Magnus
Description: A squat with the barbell racked across the front shoulders, emphasizing the quadriceps and requiring an upright torso.
Help: 1. Rest the bar across your front shoulders, elbows high, fingertips light on the bar. 2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, brace your core. 3. Squat down keeping your torso as upright as possible. 4. Drive through your heels to stand back up. Tip: Keep your elbows up throughout; dropping them tips the bar forward.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Glutes
Description: A squat holding a single dumbbell or kettlebell at chest height, training quads and glutes while teaching good squat form.
Help: 1. Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest. 2. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width. 3. Squat down, letting elbows brush inside your knees. 4. Drive through your heels to stand back up. Tip: Keep your chest tall and elbows close to the weight for balance.

Tags: Legs, Hamstrings, Gluteus Maximus, Erector Spinae
Description: A hip-hinge exercise with a barbell on the back that stretches and strengthens the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back.
Help: 1. Rest a barbell on your upper back like a squat. 2. Stand with feet hip-width apart, soft knees. 3. Hinge at the hips, pushing your glutes back as your torso lowers. 4. Reverse the motion by driving your hips forward to stand tall. Tip: Keep your back flat and use a light weight until your hip-hinge pattern is solid.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Glutes
Description: A machine-based squat performed on an angled sled, targeting the quadriceps with strong back support.
Help: 1. Load the sled and position your shoulders and back against the pads. 2. Place feet shoulder-width apart on the platform. 3. Release the safety and bend your knees to lower the sled. 4. Push through your feet to extend back up. Tip: Don't let your lower back round off the pad at the bottom.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
Description: A deadlift performed inside a hexagonal bar, training the quads, glutes, and hamstrings with a more upright torso than a straight bar.
Help: 1. Stand inside the hex bar with feet hip-width apart. 2. Bend hips and knees to grip the handles, chest up, back flat. 3. Drive through your feet to stand up, keeping the bar close to your body. 4. Reverse the motion to lower it back down. Tip: Keep the bar path vertical and avoid rounding your lower back.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Medius, Gluteus Minimus
Description: A seated machine exercise that pushes the thighs outward against resistance, isolating the outer glutes.
Help: 1. Sit in the machine with legs against the pads. 2. Push your knees outward against the resistance. 3. Pause briefly at the widest point. 4. Return under control to the start. Tip: Avoid bouncing; use a controlled tempo to keep tension on the glutes.

Tags: Legs, Adductors
Description: A seated machine exercise that squeezes the thighs together against resistance, targeting the inner thigh adductors.
Help: 1. Sit in the machine with legs spread against the outer pads. 2. Squeeze your legs together against the resistance. 3. Pause briefly at the innermost point. 4. Return slowly to the start. Tip: Move through a controlled range and avoid slamming the pads together.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Maximus, Quadriceps
Description: A step-up performed sideways onto a raised platform, working the glutes and quads with an emphasis on hip stability.
Help: 1. Stand sideways next to a box with one foot on top. 2. Push through that foot to step up sideways. 3. Bring the trailing leg up to standing on the box. 4. Step back down with control and repeat. Tip: Keep your hips level and avoid twisting your torso as you step up.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Rectus Femoris, Vastus Lateralis, Vastus Medialis
Description: A seated machine isolation exercise that extends the knees against resistance, directly targeting the quadriceps.
Help: 1. Sit in the machine with the pad resting on your lower shins. 2. Grip the side handles and keep your back against the seat. 3. Extend your knees to lift the pad until legs are straight. 4. Lower with control back to the start. Tip: Avoid locking out explosively; slow the top and bottom of each rep.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Glutes
Description: A machine compound exercise pressing a weighted platform with the legs, training quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
Help: 1. Sit in the machine with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform. 2. Release the safety catches. 3. Bend your knees to lower the platform toward your chest. 4. Press through your feet to extend back to the start. Tip: Don't let your lower back round off the seat as knees approach your chest.

Tags: Legs, Hamstrings, Biceps Femoris, Semitendinosus
Description: A prone machine isolation exercise that curls the ankles toward the glutes, targeting the hamstrings.
Help: 1. Lie face down with the pad resting just above your heels. 2. Grip the handles and keep hips pressed into the bench. 3. Curl your heels up toward your glutes. 4. Lower with control back to the start. Tip: Keep your hips flat on the pad; lifting them reduces hamstring tension.

Tags: Legs, Hamstrings, Biceps Femoris, Semitendinosus
Description: A bodyweight hamstring exercise where you lower your torso forward from kneeling while anchored at the ankles.
Help: 1. Kneel with ankles secured under a pad or partner's hands. 2. Keep your body straight from knees to head. 3. Slowly lower your torso forward as far as you can control with your hamstrings. 4. Push off the floor or pull yourself back up using your hamstrings. Tip: Start with a small range of motion; this is an advanced, very demanding exercise.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings
Description: A lunge stepping backward instead of forward, training quads, glutes, and hamstrings with less knee stress than a forward lunge.
Help: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. 2. Step one leg backward and lower your hips. 3. Bend both knees until the back knee nears the floor. 4. Push through the front heel to return to standing. Tip: Keep your front shin close to vertical to protect the front knee.

Tags: Legs, Hamstrings, Biceps Femoris, Gluteus Maximus, Glutes
Description: A hip-hinge exercise holding weight while keeping the legs fairly straight, primarily targeting the hamstrings and glutes.
Help: 1. Hold a barbell or dumbbells in front of your thighs. 2. Stand with a slight bend in the knees. 3. Hinge at the hips, pushing them back as the weight lowers along your legs. 4. Feel a hamstring stretch, then drive hips forward to stand. Tip: Keep the bar close to your legs and your back flat throughout.

Tags: Legs, Calves, Soleus
Description: A seated machine exercise pressing through the balls of the feet with bent knees, isolating the soleus calf muscle.
Help: 1. Sit in the machine with knees under the pad and balls of feet on the platform. 2. Let your heels drop for a full stretch. 3. Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels. 4. Lower slowly back down. Tip: Use a full range of motion and pause briefly at the top for better contraction.

Tags: Legs, Hamstrings, Biceps Femoris, Semitendinosus
Description: A seated machine isolation exercise that curls the ankles toward the seat, targeting the hamstrings.
Help: 1. Sit in the machine with the pad against the back of your lower legs. 2. Secure the thigh pad and grip the handles. 3. Curl your legs down and back by bending your knees. 4. Return slowly to the starting position. Tip: Keep your back against the pad and avoid using momentum to move the weight.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Medius, Gluteus Minimus
Description: A floor-based exercise lying on your side that opens the top knee like a clamshell, targeting the outer glutes.
Help: 1. Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked, hips stacked. 2. Keep feet together and lift your top knee open. 3. Pause at the top of the movement. 4. Lower with control and repeat. Tip: Keep your hips still and avoid rolling your pelvis backward to cheat the range.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus
Description: An advanced single-leg squat performed on one leg with the other extended forward, building unilateral quad and glute strength plus balance.
Help: 1. Stand on one leg, extending the other leg straight out in front. 2. Bend the standing knee and hip to lower down. 3. Keep the raised leg off the floor throughout. 4. Push through the standing heel to return to standing. Tip: Use a support or box under you at first to build strength and balance safely.

Tags: Legs, Calves, Gastrocnemius, Soleus
Description: A standing exercise raising the heels against resistance with straight legs, targeting the gastrocnemius calf muscle.
Help: 1. Stand with balls of feet on a raised platform, heels hanging off. 2. Let your heels drop down for a full stretch. 3. Press through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes. 4. Lower slowly back down. Tip: Move through a full range of motion rather than small, quick pulses.

Tags: Legs, Glutes, Gluteus Maximus, Quadriceps
Description: A single-leg exercise stepping onto a raised platform, training the glutes and quadriceps while building unilateral strength.
Help: 1. Stand facing a sturdy box or bench with one foot on top. 2. Push through that foot to step fully onto the box. 3. Bring the trailing leg up to standing. 4. Step back down with control and repeat. Tip: Drive through the heel of the stepping foot rather than pushing off the trailing leg.

Tags: Legs, Quadriceps, Gluteus Maximus, Hamstrings, Glutes
Description: A lunge performed while moving forward step by step, training quads, glutes, and hamstrings along with balance and coordination.
Help: 1. Stand tall and step forward with one leg into a lunge. 2. Lower until both knees are bent near 90 degrees. 3. Push through the front heel to bring the back leg forward into the next lunge. 4. Continue alternating legs as you move forward. Tip: Keep your torso upright and take controlled, not overly long, strides.

Tags: Legs, Calves, Shins, Tibialis Anterior
Description: An exercise lifting the toes upward against resistance, strengthening the tibialis anterior muscle on the front of the shin.
Help: 1. Lean your back against a wall with heels a foot or so out in front. 2. Rest weight (like a plate) on top of your feet, or use a band. 3. Lift your toes and forefoot up toward your shins. 4. Lower with control back down. Tip: Keep your heels planted and move only at the ankle joint.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis, Transverse Abdominis, Obliques
Description: A kneeling core exercise rolling a wheel forward and back, heavily challenging the abs and deep core stabilizers.
Help: 1. Kneel on the floor holding the ab wheel with both hands. 2. Brace your core and roll the wheel forward, extending your body. 3. Go as far as you can control without your hips sagging. 4. Pull back through your abs to return to start. Tip: Keep your back flat; stop the rollout before your lower back arches.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis
Description: A kneeling cable exercise crunching the torso downward against resistance, targeting the rectus abdominis.
Help: 1. Kneel below a high cable with a rope attachment, holding it by your head. 2. Keep your hips fixed in place. 3. Crunch your torso down, curling your spine toward your hips. 4. Slowly return to the start. Tip: Move from your abs, not your arms or hips, and keep the motion controlled.

Tags: Core, Obliques, Rectus Abdominis
Description: A rotational cable exercise pulling the handle diagonally across the body, training the obliques and rotational core strength.
Help: 1. Set the cable high or low and stand sideways to the machine. 2. Grip the handle with both hands. 3. Rotate your torso and pull the handle across your body. 4. Return with control and repeat, then switch sides. Tip: Rotate through your torso and hips, not just your arms.

Tags: Core, Transverse Abdominis, Rectus Abdominis, Obliques
Description: A slow floor exercise moving opposite arm and leg while lying on your back, training core stability and coordination.
Help: 1. Lie on your back with arms reaching up and knees bent at 90 degrees. 2. Brace your core to flatten your lower back into the floor. 3. Slowly extend one arm overhead and the opposite leg out straight. 4. Return and repeat on the other side. Tip: Keep your lower back pressed to the floor the entire time; stop the range if it lifts.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis, Hip Flexors
Description: A hanging exercise lifting bent knees toward the chest, targeting the lower abs and hip flexors.
Help: 1. Hang from a pull-up bar with arms straight. 2. Brace your core to stop swinging. 3. Raise your knees up toward your chest. 4. Lower with control back to the start. Tip: Avoid swinging; use your abs to initiate the movement rather than momentum.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis, Hip Flexors, Lower Abs
Description: A hanging exercise lifting straight legs upward, strongly targeting the lower abs and hip flexors.
Help: 1. Hang from a pull-up bar with arms straight and legs extended. 2. Brace your core to stop swinging. 3. Raise your straight legs up toward hip height or higher. 4. Lower with control back to the start. Tip: Keep the movement slow and controlled to avoid swinging on the bar.

Tags: Core, Transverse Abdominis, Obliques
Description: An anti-rotation cable exercise pressing a handle straight out from the chest, training core stability against rotation.
Help: 1. Stand sideways to a cable machine, handle held at your chest. 2. Brace your core to resist the pull toward the machine. 3. Press the handle straight out in front of you. 4. Return with control back to your chest. Tip: Keep your hips and shoulders square; don't let the cable twist your torso.

Tags: Core, Transverse Abdominis, Rectus Abdominis, Obliques
Description: A static hold on forearms and toes that builds isometric strength and endurance in the core and shoulders.
Help: 1. Rest on your forearms and toes, elbows under shoulders. 2. Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels. 3. Brace your core and squeeze your glutes. 4. Hold the position for the target time while breathing steadily. Tip: Don't let your hips sag or pike up; keep the line straight.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis
Description: A floor exercise curling the hips and knees up toward the chest, emphasizing the lower rectus abdominis.
Help: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet off the floor. 2. Keep your arms flat by your sides for support. 3. Curl your hips up, bringing your knees toward your chest. 4. Lower with control without letting feet touch down. Tip: Use your abs to curl the hips, not momentum from swinging the legs.

Tags: Core, Obliques
Description: A seated rotational exercise twisting the torso side to side, targeting the obliques and rotational core strength.
Help: 1. Sit with knees bent, leaning back slightly, feet lifted or on the floor. 2. Hold your hands together or a weight in front of your chest. 3. Rotate your torso to tap the floor on one side. 4. Rotate to the other side and repeat. Tip: Move slowly and control the rotation; don't just swing your arms.

Tags: Core, Obliques, Transverse Abdominis
Description: A static hold on one forearm and the side of the foot that builds lateral core strength, especially the obliques.
Help: 1. Lie on your side, propped on one forearm, elbow under your shoulder. 2. Stack your feet and lift your hips off the floor. 3. Keep your body in a straight line from head to feet. 4. Hold the position, then repeat on the other side. Tip: Don't let your hips drop; keep them lifted and in line with your shoulders.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis, Hip Flexors
Description: A classic floor exercise raising the torso fully upright from lying down, training the abs and hip flexors.
Help: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, hands lightly behind your head or crossed on chest. 2. Brace your core. 3. Curl and lift your torso all the way up toward your knees. 4. Lower with control back to the floor. Tip: Avoid yanking your neck with your hands; let your abs do the lifting.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis
Description: A basic floor exercise curling the shoulders off the ground, isolating the upper rectus abdominis.
Help: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat. 2. Place hands lightly behind your head or crossed on your chest. 3. Curl your shoulders up off the floor, contracting your abs. 4. Lower with control back down. Tip: Keep your lower back on the floor and avoid pulling on your neck.

Tags: Core, Rectus Abdominis, Hip Flexors
Description: A floor exercise simultaneously raising the torso and legs to form a V shape, working the entire rectus abdominis and hip flexors.
Help: 1. Lie flat on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight. 2. Brace your core. 3. Simultaneously lift your torso and legs, reaching hands toward your toes. 4. Lower with control back to the start. Tip: Keep your legs and arms straight throughout to maximize the range of motion.
